To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel component of bacterial microcompart-ments and have determined its structure and biochemical function.
the AAA+ protein CsoCbbC is part of the α-carboxysomes and is required for carboxysomes to form.
the CbbQ proteins are a novel class of carboxysome components and that they hydrolyze ATP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of a new protein component of carboxysomes.
the structural and functional characterization of a newly identified component of α-carboxysomes: the AAA+ domain protein CsoCbbC.
the structural characterization of a new carboxysome component and the identification of the first example of a bacterial microcomp-partment-associated ATPase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CsoCBBQ is the first example of an AAA+ domain protein associated with a bacterial organelle.
CbbQ is a novel protein component of the α-carboxysomes, which may play an important role in their assembly and/or maintenance.
CsoCBBQ is a novel carboxysome component that is part of the carboxy-some shell and has ATPase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CsoCBBQ is a novel component of α-carboxysomes that is required for carboxysomal biogenesis.
the CbbQ ATPase, CsoC, is a novel component of α-carboxysomes and that it is a hexamer with a distinct hexagonal shape.
the α-Carboxyome is a newly identified bacterial microcompartment that has an expanded gene locus, and contains a CbbO and a CbbQ ATPase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CbbQ and CbbO are components of α-carboxysomes, and the ATPase CbbQ may play a role in the biogenesis and/or function of the shell.
